Q: How can I open a file for both reading and writing? A:

r+ is the canonical mode for reading and writing at the same time. This is not different from using the fopen() system call (man fopen), since Python's file() and open() are just a tiny wrappers around this operating system call.

Q: `git` upstream dependency narrowing A:

Use sparse checkout:

[git sparse-checkout init --cone] (optional in new versions)

git sparse-checkout set src/module1 src/module4 src/tests docs
git sparse-checkout add src/module{10..19}

In new Git versions, sparse checkout defaults to "cone" mode where you list whole subtrees you want to keep. It is still possible to use the non-cone mode which will allow you to use more finegrained 'gitignore'-style inclusions and !exclusions.

git sparse-checkout init --no-cone

git sparse-checkout set "/src/module*" "/docs/*.md" "/tests" "!/tests/useless"

(Note that 1) non-cone mode is slower with large repositories, 2) non-cone mode expects raw gitignore-style filters where paths start with /.)
